title: Modern History: Leaders of Freedom Movement (Test)

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statement is/are correct?

I. Mahatma Gandhi introduced the concept of Satyagraha in India during the Champaran movement.

II. The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
questions.solution_en:
· Mahatma Gandhi introduced Satyagraha in India through the Champaran Movement (1917) to support indigo farmers.

· The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922) was launched as a response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Rowlatt Act.
questions.solution_hi:
· Mahatma Gandhi introduced Satyagraha in India through the Champaran Movement (1917) to support indigo farmers.

· The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922) was launched as a response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Rowlatt Act.

I. Dadabhai Naoroji propounded the "Drain of Wealth" theory in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India."

II. Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1915.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statement is/are correct?

I. Subhas Chandra Bose founded the Forward Bloc in 1939 after resigning from the Congress.

II. The Indian National Army (INA) was originally formed in 1942 under Mohan Singh, but later led by Bose.
questions.solution_en:
· Subhas Chandra Bose founded the Forward Bloc in 1939 after resigning from the Indian National Congress due to ideological differences with Mahatma Gandhi and the Congress leadership.

· The Indian National Army (INA) was initially formed in 1942 under the leadership of Captain Mohan Singh, with the help of the Japanese in Southeast Asia. Later, Subhas Chandra Bose took over its leadership in 1943 and revitalized it as a significant force in the fight for India's independence.
questions.solution_hi:
· Subhas Chandra Bose founded the Forward Bloc in 1939 after resigning from the Indian National Congress due to ideological differences with Mahatma Gandhi and the Congress leadership.

· The Indian National Army (INA) was initially formed in 1942 under the leadership of Captain Mohan Singh, with the help of the Japanese in Southeast Asia. Later, Subhas Chandra Bose took over its leadership in 1943 and revitalized it as a significant force in the fight for India's independence.

i. Raja Ram Mohan Roya. Abolition of Sati
ii. Jyotiba Phuleb. Women's Education
iii. Dr. B.R. Ambedkarc. Architect of Indian Constitution
iv. Swami Vivekanandad. Spread of Vedanta philosophy
questions.solution_en:
Raja Ram Mohan Roy → a. Abolition of Sati

He was a key social reformer who campaigned against the inhumane practice of Sati and helped bring about its abolition in 1829.

Jyotiba Phule → b. Women's Education

Phule, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, pioneered efforts in promoting education for girls and lower castes.

Dr. B.R. Ambedkar → c. Architect of Indian Constitution

He was the principal architect of the Indian Constitution and a champion for Dalit rights and social justice.

Swami Vivekananda → d. Spread of Vedanta philosophy

Through his speeches, especially at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago (1893), he popularized Vedanta and Indian philosophy globally.

Match the movement with its leader:

Column A (Movement)Column B (Leader)
i. Civil Disobedience Movementa. Mahatma Gandhi
ii. Quit India Movementb. Mahatma Gandhi
iii. Swadeshi Movementc. Bipin Chandra Pal
iv. Home Rule Movementd. Annie Besant
questions.solution_en:
· Civil Disobedience Movement → a. Mahatma Gandhi

Launched in 1930, this movement involved nonviolent refusal to obey British laws, including the famous Salt March.

· Quit India Movement → b. Mahatma Gandhi

Started in 1942, Gandhi gave the call to "Do or Die" urging the British to leave India immediately.

· Swadeshi Movement → c. Bipin Chandra Pal

Part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio, Bipin Chandra Pal was a key leader in promoting the Swadeshi Movement (1905), encouraging Indians to boycott British goods.

· Home Rule Movement → d. Annie Besant

Annie Besant, along with Bal Gangadhar Tilak, was instrumental in demanding self-governance for India through this movement in 1916.

I. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of Independent India.

II. Vallabhbhai Patel played a crucial role in the integration of princely states into India.

· Vallabhbhai Patel was known as the "Iron Man of India" and played a key role in integrating princely states.

o Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister, played a key role in integrating over 500 princely states into the Indian Union after independence.

I. Chandra Shekhar Azad - Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)

II. Ram Prasad Bismil - Assembly Bombing Case

III.Bhagat Singh - Kakori Train Robbery
questions.solution_en:
I. Chandra Shekhar Azad - Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) is Correct

Chandra Shekhar Azad was a prominent leader of the HSRA, a revolutionary organization that aimed to overthrow British rule.

II. Ram Prasad Bismil - Assembly Bombing Case is Incorrect

Ram Prasad Bismil was not involved in the Assembly Bombing Case. He was a key figure in the Kakori Train Robbery (1925), not the Assembly Bombing.

III. Bhagat Singh - Kakori Train Robbery is Incorrect

Bhagat Singh was not involved in the Kakori Train Robbery. That event took place in 1925, when Bhagat Singh was still quite young and not yet associated with revolutionary activities. He later became known for the Assembly Bombing Case (1929) and the Saunders assassination.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statement is/are correct?

I. The Simon Commission was boycotted because it did not include any Indian members.

II. Lala Lajpat Rai succumbed to injuries sustained during a protest against the Simon Commission.
questions.solution_en:
· The Simon Commission (1927) was an all-British commission set up to recommend constitutional reforms in India. Indians boycotted it widely because no Indian was included in the commission.

· During a protest against the commission in Lahore (1928), Lala Lajpat Rai was brutally lathi-charged by police. He sustained serious injuries and died shortly after, leading to widespread outrage.

questions.q_en: Who is known as the "Iron Man of India"?
questions.solution_en:
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel earned the title "Iron Man of India" for his strong leadership and decisive role in the integration of over 500 princely states into the Indian Union after independence.

His firmness and resolve in unifying the nation earned him this title.

questions.q_en: Who was the first Indian to demand 'Poorna Swaraj' (Complete Independence)?
questions.solution_en:
Dadabhai Naoroji was one of the earliest leaders to demand complete independence from British rule.

In 1906, he used the term "Swaraj" during the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress, and although others later popularized the call for "Poorna Swaraj," he was the first to articulate the concept publicly.

questions.q_en: Who was popularly known as 'Lokmanya'?
questions.solution_en:
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was given the honorary title "Lokmanya," meaning "accepted by the people (as their leader)."

He was a prominent freedom fighter who asserted, "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it."

His fiery speeches and writings inspired a generation of Indians to join the freedom struggle.

He established Deccan Education Society in Pune.

questions.q_en: Who was called the "Grand Old Man of India"?
questions.solution_en:
Dadabhai Naoroji was referred to as the "Grand Old Man of India" due to his long and dedicated service to the Indian freedom struggle.

He was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress and the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament.

His economic critique of British rule, particularly the "Drain Theory," laid an intellectual foundation for the nationalist movement.

Further information:

Gopal Krishna Gokhale (1866 - 1915)

· Moderate Leader: Advocated constitutional reforms and dialogue with the British.

· Servants of India Society (1905): Founded to promote social service, education, and self-reliance.

· Remembered as the "Political Guru of Gandhi" and a bridge between moderates and extremists.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856 - 1920):

"Father of Indian Unrest"; pioneered mass nationalism with slogans like "Swaraj is my birthright" and organized Ganesh Chaturthi/Shivaji festivals to unite Indians against British rule.

Lala Lajpat Rai (1865 - 1928):

"Punjab Kesari" (Lion of Punjab); led anti-Simon Commission protests (1928) and inspired revolutionary nationalism, co-founding the extremist Lal-Bal-Pal trio with Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal.

questions.q_en: Who led the Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution_en:
C. . Rajagopalachari, a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi, led the Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu.

He organized a march from Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam in 1930, mirroring Gandhi's Dandi March.

This act of civil disobedience was a major milestone in the Indian independence movement in South India.

questions.q_en: Who founded the Rani Jhansi Regiment (1943), the women's wing of the Azad Hind Fauj?
questions.solution_en:
Captain Lakshmi Sahgal founded and led the Rani Jhansi Regiment, the women's wing of Subhas Chandra Bose's Indian National Army (INA), in 1943.

The regiment was named after Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi and symbolized women's active role in the freedom struggle.

Captain Lakshmi was a trailblazer in promoting women's participation in India's fight for independence.

questions.q_en: Who gave the slogan "Give me blood and I shall give you freedom"?
questions.solution_en:
· Subhas Chandra Bose, a prominent freedom fighter and leader of the Indian National Army (INA), gave the powerful slogan "Give me blood and I shall give you freedom" in 1944 during a speech to Indians in Burma.

· The slogan was a call to arms, urging Indians to join the struggle for complete independence from British rule through direct action.

questions.q_en: Who led the tribal rebellion in Andhra Pradesh known as the Rampa Rebellion (1922 - 24)?
questions.solution_en:
· Alluri Sitarama Raju was the charismatic leader of the Rampa Rebellion (also known as the Manyam Rebellion) in the Eastern Ghats region of Andhra Pradesh.

· He organized and led tribal communities in an armed uprising against British colonial rule, particularly in protest against the repressive Forest Laws.

· Raju is celebrated as "Manyam Veerudu" (Hero of the Jungle) in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

questions.q_en: Which regional leader from Tamil Nadu played a key role in the Vaikom Satyagraha?
questions.solution_en:
· E. V. Ramasamy, popularly known as Periyar, played a crucial role in supporting the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924 - 25), a nonviolent movement in Kerala demanding access for lower castes to roads around the Vaikom temple.

· Periyar's involvement gave the movement national visibility and earned him the title "Vaikom Veerar" (Hero of Vaikom).

· His efforts marked a significant step in the anti-caste and social reform movements in South India.
